Atlanta Braves legend turned broadcaster John Smoltz made an error while recognizing Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Trevor Megill during World Series Game 1 against the Tampa Bay Rays. Megill induced a game-ending double play to help Milwaukee escape with what was thought to be a 3-1 victory. However, the call on second was overturned, requiring Megill to return to the mound and secure the final out in the Brewers' 3-2 victory.
 During the Fox broadcast, Hall of Fame commentator Smoltz described Brewers closer Megill as a former New York Mets starter. The former Braves pitcher might have confused Trevor with his brother, Tylor Megill, who pitched for the Mets.
 Fans on X called out Smoltz over the error, particularly because it happened during the World Series, when broadcasters are expected to be well prepared.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "This #WorldSeries booth is brutal. Embarrassing for Smoltz to call Trevor Megill a "former Mets starter, now Brewers closer" confusing him with Tylor. This is a brutal booth but because it's John Smoltz, it doesn't matter. Embarrassing on a World Series broadcast," one fan wrote.
 Here are more reactions:
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Trevor Megill Comes Through For Brewers Twice In Same Inning
 Milwaukee led 3-1 entering the ninth inning. With one out, Megill was successful in inducing a ground ball off Rays slugger Liam Hicks. Brice Turang threw the ball to shortstop Cooper Pratt for the play at second base, and then Pratt fired the throw to first to complete the double play.
 The Rays asked for the call to be replayed, and it was found that Pratt's foot came off the second base while collecting the throw. As a result, the call was overturned, and the Brewers closer had to do it once again.
 "I just kind of looked at one of the umpires there and said, 'Hey, what are you hearing in your ear?'" Megill said via The New York Times . "He said, 'Uh, whatever, not too good. Do you want to throw some baseballs?'"
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Rays put the tying run in scoring position after the game-ending double play call was overturned. Megill returned and struck out Jonny DeLuca to secure the Brewers' 3-2 win.
 "It's tense," Megill said. "It's a situation that demands perfection or grit; more grit than the other person, at least. So I don't know, man. It's just kind of one of those spots that, you know — it's time to cook."
 Megill has established himself as a proven winner for Milwaukee this October. He has nailed all five save situations and holds a 1-0 record with an ERA of 1.35 and seven strikeouts in the 2026 postseason.
